title: The second Adams operator multiplies the Chern classes and the Chern character by powers of two
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over (S, delta), with psi^2 as in Lemma labelled lemma-second-adams-operator and c and ch as in Remarks labelled remark-chern-classes-K and remark-chern-character-K, the lemma asserts c_i(psi^2(alpha)) = 2^i c_i(alpha) and ch_i(psi^2(alpha)) = 2^i ch_i(alpha) for all alpha in K_0(Vect(X)) (statement lines 12901-12910). The proof observes that multiplying by 2^i in degree i is a ring map of the product of the A^i(X), so since psi^2 is also a ring map it suffices to check the formulas on additive generators, i.e. on classes [E] of finite locally free modules, and by the construction of the Chern classes one may assume E has constant rank r by Remark labelled remark-extend-to-finite-locally-free (proof lines 12912-12922). The splitting principle, Lemma labelled lemma-splitting-principle, then supplies a projective smooth p : P -> X with A^*(X) -> A^*(P) injective such that p^*E has a finite filtration with invertible graded parts L_j; writing x_j = c_1(L_j) the proof computes c(alpha) = prod (1 + x_j) and c(psi^2(alpha)) = prod (1 + 2x_j), and ch(alpha) = sum exp(x_j) with ch(psi^2(alpha)) = sum exp(2x_j), from which the two formulas follow (proof lines 12924-12942). Recognising that the multiplicative structure reduces the statement to line bundles, and then reading the effect of psi^2 off the splitting of E, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
